posts.title: US blacklists Megaspeed, the chip firm tied to the Nvidia scandal
posts.summary: The Commerce Department added Singapore-based Megaspeed and six linked companies in Singapore, Malaysia and Thailand to its Entity List over the risk of advanced AI chips being diverted to unauthorized users. US companies now need a license to sell to them.

links.label: The Hill: Commerce adds Megaspeed to trade blacklist

posts.title: Sanofi is buying US drugmaker Insmed for $41 billion
posts.summary: Sanofi agreed to pay $175 a share in cash for New Jersey-based Insmed, maker of the lung-disease drug Brinsupri. The deal still needs shareholder and regulatory approval and is expected to close in the first half of 2027.

posts.title: Don't panic if ICE stops you: 4 things to do
posts.summary: Stay calm, use your right to stay silent and ask for a lawyer, never lie or sign what you don't understand, and if you have valid papers, show them when an immigration officer asks. Noncitizens over 18 are required to carry their immigration documents.

links.label: ACLU: Know Your Rights for immigrants

posts.title: Industries using AI most are hiring fewer beginners, report finds
posts.summary: A Burning Glass Institute and RAISE US report finds the share of postings open to people with 3 years of experience or less fell 3-8% below average in the most AI-intensive industries, while jobs AI mainly helps grew by about 1.4 million from 2023 to 2025.

links.label: Burning Glass Institute: Fewer Rungs, New Bridges

posts.title: Nvidia adds about $950 billion in one day, the biggest one-day gain on record
posts.summary: Nvidia shares closed up about 31% on Monday after its board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, adding roughly $950 billion in market value. That is more than double the previous one-day record, Microsoft's ~$450 billion gain on July 30.

posts.title: South Korea's education minister resigns over AI exam-cheating scandal
posts.summary: Choi Kyo-jin resigned after criticism of last-minute anti-AI-cheating measures for the national college entrance exam, which followed a tax accountant exam top scorer's admission to cheating with a hidden camera, a smartphone and AI. The ministry reported 111 suspected device breaches on exam day.

posts.title: Massachusetts sues ICE over 38 courthouse arrests
posts.summary: Attorney General Andrea Campbell filed a federal lawsuit in Boston saying ICE made at least 38 civil arrests in state courthouses without judicial warrants since the PROTECT Act's courthouse rule took effect on Nov 3. The suit challenges a May 2025 ICE directive; DHS has pointed to the Supremacy Clause.

posts.title: OpenAI's chief scientist proposes industry-wide limits on powerful AI
posts.summary: Jakub Pachocki proposed that AI companies agree on common limits, based on perplexity and other measures, that they would not cross until AI behavior can be better understood and monitored. CEO Sam Altman backed the proposal; it is not a rule.

posts.title: A system glitch delayed more than 1,300 Delta flights as Thanksgiving travel began
posts.summary: On Sunday, Delta's weight-and-balance system went down, delaying more than 1,300 flights nationwide, mostly at Atlanta. Delta says the system is restored, it was not a hack, and it is rebooking travelers and refunding canceled flights.

posts.title: Amazon confirms deal for Decart's AI chip tech, reported at $7.5 billion
posts.summary: Amazon signed an agreement to buy the technology behind the Decart Optimization Stack and bring Decart's co-founders and AI team on board. Amazon didn't disclose the price; Bloomberg reports about $7.5 billion, and the deal still needs regulatory clearance.

posts.title: Nasdaq jumps about 7% after its worst week since 2020
posts.summary: US stocks rebounded sharply Monday morning, led by tech and AI shares, after all three major indexes ended last week in correction territory. Nvidia rose about 30% after reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO.

posts.title: Nvidia brings back Jensen Huang as CEO, 11 days after he resigned
posts.summary: Nvidia's board voted unanimously on Monday to reinstate Jensen Huang as president, CEO and board member, effective immediately, after saying last week it did not plan to. An independent directors' investigation will continue, and Colette Kress returns to her CFO role.

links.label: Fox Business: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO

posts.title: CrowdStrike is buying Zscaler for $43.9 billion
posts.summary: CrowdStrike and Zscaler announced on Monday an all-stock deal valuing Zscaler at about $43.9 billion, one of the largest cybersecurity deals on record. Zscaler holders get 1.135 CrowdStrike shares each, a 34% premium; the deal still needs approvals.

links.label: CNBC (Reuters): CrowdStrike bets on network security with Zscaler deal

posts.title: 4 ways to stay in the US after OPT ends
posts.summary: O-1, Day-1 CPT, H-1B with cap-gap, and the STEM OPT extension. The catch: STEM OPT must be filed within 90 days before your OPT end date and received by USCIS before it expires.

posts.title: US Treasury chief: we need answers from Nvidia on China chip sales
posts.summary: On CBS's Face the Nation on Sunday, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the US is seeking answers from Nvidia on its chip sales to China and wants to know who ran compliance. Nvidia stock fell about 23% last week.

links.label: Reuters via MarketScreener: US seeks answers on Nvidia chip sales to China
Reuters via U.S. News: Bessent on Nvidia

posts.title: ICE arrested 2 passengers boarding a flight at Seattle's airport
posts.summary: On Nov 21, ICE made an arrest on an Alaska Airlines jet bridge at Sea-Tac as passengers boarded a flight to Los Angeles. DHS says both people arrested had overstayed visas; Washington's governor and the Port of Seattle criticized the operation.

links.label: KUOW/OPB: Port officials react to Sea-Tac ICE arrest
Fox News: DHS, officials clash after Seattle airport arrest

posts.title: Intel's workforce shrank by 7,300 in a year as sales rose 21%
posts.summary: Intel reported about 81,100 employees as of Sept 26, 2026, down from 88,400 a year earlier, while Q3 revenue rose 21% to $16.5 billion. A Nov 16 California WARN notice adds 57 more cuts in Santa Clara, including engineering roles.

posts.title: Amazon reportedly near a $7.5B deal for 2-year-old AI startup Decart
posts.summary: The Financial Times reported that Amazon is in final-stage talks to buy Decart, an AI startup founded in 2023, for about $7.5 billion; a deal could come as soon as early next week but could still fall apart. Decart was valued at $4 billion in May and was an early user of Amazon's Trainium AI chips.

links.label: TipRanks: Amazon eyes $7.5 billion AI startup deal
Seeking Alpha: Amazon nears $7.5B deal to buy Decart (FT)

posts.title: US spy chief: China likely got Nvidia's top AI chips
posts.summary: Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton said in Sunday TV interviews that he expects China found ways to obtain Nvidia's most advanced AI chips despite export limits. Treasury has given Nvidia until Nov 25 to say whether restricted chips reached China through shell companies.

links.label: CNN: DNI Clayton says China likely obtained Nvidia AI chips
ABC News: This Week transcript, Nov 22
Yahoo News: Treasury still waiting for answers from Nvidia

posts.title: Anthropic's IPO bankers: no OpenAI work for 6 months
posts.summary: A Reuters report says Anthropic asked senior bankers on its record IPO not to work for rivals such as OpenAI for 6 months. The stock, priced at $83, closed day one at $97.17 and slid about 8.5% on Friday in the AI sell-off.

links.label: Fox News Digital live updates (citing Reuters)

posts.title: December grads: file your OPT before you fly home
posts.summary: USCIS must receive a post-completion OPT application between 90 days before and 60 days after your I-20 program end date, within 30 days of your DSO's SEVIS recommendation, and you must file from inside the US. For a Dec 15, 2026 end date, the last day is Feb 13, 2027.

links.label: ASU ISSC: Apply early for post-OPT

posts.title: A $1,700 tax credit for scholarship donations comes to Florida in 2027
posts.summary: Florida opted in to the Federal Scholarship Tax Credit: from Jan 1, 2027, taxpayers can claim up to $1,700 a year ($3,400 married filing jointly) for cash gifts to approved K-12 Scholarship Granting Organizations. The credit is non-refundable.

posts.title: Week in 60 seconds: the 9 stories you needed
posts.summary: Anthropic's record IPO, AI stocks' worst week since 2020 and a GAO report on chatbots planning attacks; F-1 grace period and CPT court rulings and a proposed PERM rewrite; IBM ending most consulting sponsorship, Texas's H-1B freeze plan and a 9% drop in new international students.

posts.title: US investigators got 4 AI chatbots to plan attacks in under 12 hours
posts.summary: A GAO report found ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Grok each produced viable attack plans after investigators bypassed their safeguards. The companies say they keep improving safety, and Sen. Maggie Hassan plans AI hearings in January.

posts.title: Texas's next governor plans to end the state's H-1B freeze
posts.summary: Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa told The Texas Tribune she plans to scrap Gov. Abbott's pause on new H-1B petitions at state agencies and public universities, which runs through May 31, 2027. It's a plan for now; the freeze still applies until it is officially reversed.

posts.title: A test with 2 million AI prompts caught 3 AI providers hacked
posts.summary: Security firm Dragos seeded about 2 million AI prompts with bait secrets and found attackers had breached at least 3 AI hosting providers, while some resellers logged customer prompts and some ignored zero-data-retention settings. Avoid putting real passwords or API keys into AI tools.

links.label: Dragos research: Three breaches, endless leaks

posts.title: Bitcoin fell to $55,252, its lowest price in 2 years
posts.summary: Bitcoin slid to about $55,252 on Saturday, its lowest since September 2024, then bounced back near $60,000 as the AI stock selloff spilled into crypto. News only, not investment advice.

posts.title: ICE detains a Princeton PhD student at a DC airport after a science conference
posts.summary: ICE detained Princeton neuroscience PhD student Eva Yi Xie at Reagan National Airport on Nov 19 before a domestic flight. DHS says she overstayed a 2016 admission and never held student status; her lawyer says her pending asylum case lets her stay, and a federal judge has barred her transfer and ordered the government to respond by Nov 25.

links.label: NBC News: Princeton neuroscientist detained by ICE at D.C. airport
Philadelphia Inquirer: ICE arrest of a Princeton scholar mobilizes academics

posts.title: Trump threatens a 'tremendous tax' on US companies that build AI data centers abroad
posts.summary: At a White House briefing on Nov 20, President Trump said US companies won't be allowed to build data centers overseas and would face heavy penalties if they do; he gave no details on how it would be enforced. Nothing has been written into law yet.

links.label: CNBC: Trump vows to stop US companies building data centers abroad

posts.title: Math experts certify an AI-assisted proof of the 167-year-old Riemann hypothesis
posts.summary: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge says he proved the Riemann hypothesis working with Claude; the Lean and Mathlib communities certified the computer-checked proof on Nov 21. A human-readable paper and full expert review are still to come.

posts.title: Nuro is hiring 2027 new grads for Systems Engineering at up to $176K
posts.summary: Nuro (self-driving tech) is hiring a Systems Engineering New Grad 2027 in Mountain View, CA, for B.S./M.S./PhD students graduating by June 2027; posted base pay is $153,000–$176,000. The post doesn't mention visa sponsorship, so ask the recruiter.

posts.title: IBM ends visa and green card sponsorship for most IBM Consulting roles
posts.summary: IBM confirmed it will stop sponsoring US work visas and green cards for the majority of roles in IBM Consulting (150,000+ people); affected workers can work for IBM outside the US or leave by year-end, Bloomberg reported. If you apply there on OPT, check each job post's sponsorship line.

posts.title: AI stocks just had their worst week since 2020: Nasdaq down 10%
posts.summary: An AI and chip-stock sell-off pushed the Nasdaq down about 10% for the week (its worst week since March 2020) and put the S&P 500 and Dow into correction. Visa rules don't change, but tech hiring budgets can tighten when markets fall, so keep applying widely.

links.label: Fox Business: Dow, S&P 500 plunge into correction
Yahoo Finance: stock market live coverage

posts.title: DoorDash is hiring new grad software engineers (2027 start) in 5 US cities
posts.summary: Software Engineer I, Entry-Level for Fall 2026–Summer 2027 grads in Los Angeles, New York, San Francisco, Sunnyvale or Seattle; posted base pay $107,400–$158,000. The posting doesn't say whether it sponsors; the application asks if you need sponsorship (USCIS: 12 initial and 135 continuing H-1B approvals in FY2023).

posts.title: Just flew back into the US? Check your I-94 first
posts.summary: Every entry creates a new I-94 record: check that it shows F-1 (not B-2), D/S instead of a fixed date, and your correct name and birth date. CBP Deferred Inspection sites can correct errors made at entry.

posts.title: International student numbers fell 9% this fall, and OPT dipped too
posts.summary: IIE's Fall 2026 Snapshot (809 schools) shows total international students down 9%, graduate down 15% and OPT down 6%; Open Doors 2026 counted 1,146,163 students last year (down 3%), with India still the top sending country. The reports don't change any F-1, OPT or CPT rule.

posts.title: Sierra is hiring new grad software engineers (2027) in San Francisco and New York
posts.summary: Software Engineer, Agent (New Grad 2027): on-site in San Francisco or New York, posted pay $160K–$190K plus equity, no deadline listed. The posting does not mention visa sponsorship, so ask the recruiter early.

posts.title: Microsoft's CEO: work is being reorganized around AI, not replaced by it
posts.summary: Microsoft offered a voluntary exit to about 60,000 eligible employees (it expects under 5% to accept), and CEO Satya Nadella says engineers will spend more time directing and reviewing AI agents. For job seekers, it means interviews and resumes that show real work done with AI tools.

links.label: Official Microsoft Blog: Voluntary Exit Offer

posts.title: The Labor Dept. wants to rewrite PERM, the first step of most work green cards
posts.summary: DOL proposed 90-day job ads, online recruiting with pay ranges, a 2-year PERM pause after related layoffs, and an end to Schedule A. It's a proposal, not law: current rules apply while comments are open for 60 days.

links.label: U.S. Department of Labor: Foreign Labor Certification

posts.title: Flying home for winter break? The 5 documents to carry
posts.summary: Passport valid 6+ months past your return, unexpired F-1 visa, I-20 with a travel signature (last 12 months; 6 on OPT), proof of spring enrollment and proof of funding. After you land, check your I-94 online.

posts.title: 3 quiet OPT mistakes, and the fix for each
posts.summary: Report your employer in the SEVP Portal within 10 days, keep your own count of unemployment days (90 on OPT, 150 total with STEM OPT), and get a travel signature that is under 6 months old before you fly.

posts.title: Flying home for winter break? Pack these 5 documents to get back in
posts.summary: Passport valid 6+ months past your return, unexpired F-1 visa, I-20 with a travel signature (under 12 months; under 6 on OPT), proof of enrollment and proof of funding. After landing, check your I-94.

posts.title: A federal judge blocked DHS's August limits on CPT
posts.summary: On 17 Nov 2026 a judge in Boston stopped DHS from enforcing two August directives that narrowed Curricular Practical Training. Schools will update their CPT policies; check with your DSO before applying. The government can still appeal.

posts.title: F-1 students keep the 60-day grace period
posts.summary: On 16 Nov 2026 a federal court vacated the DHS rule that would have ended duration of status and cut the F-1 grace period to 30 days. Duration of status stays; the grace period stays 60 days. The government can appeal.

posts.title: DHS wants to end the H-1B 60-day grace period
posts.summary: Today, H-1B workers who lose their job get up to 60 days (or until the I-94 ends) to find a new employer, change status or leave. A September 2026 proposal would remove it. It is not law yet; the 60 days still apply.

posts.title: Welcome to The Visa Clock
posts.summary: Visa news explained in plain English, who's hiring, job-search playbooks, travel and life admin. Every fact is checked against official sources, and every post shows its source and the date we checked it.
